          是的！这正是捷径的根本危险所在。一条完美的钟形曲线其「尾部极薄」。但在处理规模小、噪声大的数据集（$N=10$）时，极端随机事件的发生频率远高于完美钟形曲线的预期。正态分布低估了这些极端尾部事件的概率，从而人为地把 p 值压低。@@T5@@@@T6@@
          正是这个问题促使 Gosset 发明了「Student t 分布」—一条专为小样本设计、尾部更厚的特殊曲线。但即便如此，它仍是一种近似。@@T7@@精确置换检验@@T8@@（方法 1）不作任何假设，为你的特定数据给出绝对的真值！
@@T0@@Wait, why is the Parametric test s.src:
Wait, why is the Parametric test so different?
If you run the "New Fertilizer" or "Coffee" scenarios, you might notice the Parametric test gives a much smaller p-value than the Exact test. Did the math fail?

Yes! This is the fundamental danger of shortcuts. A perfect Bell Curve has very "thin tails." But when dealing with small, noisy datasets ($N=10$), extreme random events happen far more often than a perfect Bell Curve expects. A normal distribution underestimates the probability of these extreme tail events, artificially driving the p-value down.

This exact problem is why Gosset invented the "Student's t-distribution"—a special curve with fatter tails designed for small samples. But even that is an approximation. The Exact Permutation Test (Method 1) makes zero assumptions and gives the absolute ground truth for your specific data!

meta.title: 通过重新分组感受 p 值
meta.tagline: 用 10 个数值计算精确 p 值的迷你交互演示
meta.summary: 从两个极小的样本出发，以所有可能的方式对合并后的数值重新分组，把 p 值看作一个精确的分数，而非神秘的仪式。
highlights: 在样本相似与样本差异极大的两种情形之间切换。
查看观察到的均值差距、全部 252 种精确重新分组以及精确 p 值。
从同样的 10 个数值生成随机重新分组，并将其与观察到的分组进行比较。

Only [[[0]]] out of 252 random splits pr.zh: 252 次随机的分组中只有 [[[0]]] 次产生了这么大的差距。那只占零假设世界的 [[[1]]]%。仅凭偶然很难解释这个差距，因此我们拒绝 H\u2080，并断定该处理很可能产生了真实效果。
Only [[[0]]] out of 252 random splits pr.src: Only ${extremeSplits.length} out of 252 random splits produced a gap this large. That's just ${(pVal*100).toFixed(1)}% of the null world. It's very hard to explain this gap by chance alone, so we reject H\u2080 and conclude the treatment likely had a real effect.

[[[0]]] out of 252 random splits produce.zh: 252 次随机的分组中有 [[[0]]] 次产生了这么大或更大的差距\u2014那占零假设世界的 [[[1]]]%。大小为 [[[2]]] 的差距在纯随机下相当常见。我们无法确信该处理产生了任何效果。
[[[0]]] out of 252 random splits produce.src: ${extremeSplits.length} out of 252 random splits produced a gap this large or larger\u2014that's ${(pVal*100).toFixed(1)}% of the null world. A gap of ${state.observedGap.toFixed(1)} happens quite often by pure chance. We can't confidently say the treatment did anything.

Our gap is @@T0@@[[[0]]]@@T1@@ times lar.zh: 我们的差距是预期噪声的 @@T0@@[[[0]]]@@T1@@ 倍。它落在曲线的深处尾部。为求 p 值，我们不计数组合；我们只需用微积分求出那些极端尾部中曲线下的面积。由于 [[[1]]] 个标准差如此之远，该面积极小：@@T2@@p [[[2]]]@@T3@@。
Our gap is @@T0@@[[[0]]]@@T1@@ times lar.src: Our gap is ${zStat.toFixed(2)} times larger than the expected noise. It lands deep in the tail of the curve. To find the p-value, we don't count combinations; we just use calculus to find the area under the curve in those extreme tails. Because ${zStat.toFixed(2)} standard deviations is so far out, the area is tiny: p ${inlinePvalStr}.

Our gap is @@T0@@[[[0]]]@@T1@@ times lar.zh: 我们的差距是预期噪声的 @@T0@@[[[0]]]@@T1@@ 倍。由于 [[[1]]] 相对接近零，它落在曲线厚实的中间部分。用微积分求出尾部曲线下阴影面积，得到较大的概率：@@T2@@p [[[2]]]@@T3@@。
Our gap is @@T0@@[[[0]]]@@T1@@ times lar.src: Our gap is ${zStat.toFixed(2)} times larger than the expected noise. Because ${zStat.toFixed(2)} is relatively close to zero, it lands in the fat middle of the curve. Using calculus to find the shaded area under the curve in the tails gives us a large probability: p ${inlinePvalStr}.
